component.name: Clothbound
component.summary: Calm, local-first EPUB and PDF reader

description.p: Clothbound is a calm, local-first EPUB and PDF reader for Linux. Keep your books, academic papers, and saved web articles in one library without modifying your files, read on a quiet page, listen with built-in offline neural voices, and study with an optional local or cloud Companion.

ul.li: Local-first library with watched folders, edition grouping, collections, full-text FTS5 search, and a fast Command Palette
Zero-flash EPUB spreads and theme-recolored academic PDF reading with Fit page, Fit width, Actual size, Visual Snip & Explain, and citation peek cards
Add from URL to archive web articles offline as EPUBs, plus OPDS 1.2 and 2.0 catalog browsing
Built-in offline read-aloud voices (Kokoro, Pocket TTS, Piper) with continuous background playback, sleep timer, and M4B audiobook export
Adaptive Story and Study Companion with offline LaTeX math, plus a standalone local stdio MCP server (clothbound-mcp)
Matches desktop light and dark mode automatically and ships in 50 interface languages

description.p: Linux and Flatpak patch release adding a pruning cycle-safe library scanner for Flatpak portal folders, fixing the Flatpak file and folder picker initial directory, and making the library sidebar and reader side panels smoothly drag-resizable with persisted widths.

Universal Linux Flatpak release with live GNOME, KDE, COSMIC, and Flatpak desktop light and dark mode matching via XDG Desktop Portal, enriched diagnostics with one-click Report issue, Flatpak-aware MCP configuration, Qt 6.10 compatibility, and reader navigation and layout polish.

Architecture, reading craft, and reliability release with standalone WebEngine-free clothbound-mcp, continuous background Library audio playback, PDF viewport tiling and cursor-focal zoom, intentional desktop page turns, and 100% translation coverage across 50 languages.
Faster cold startup, kinetic trackpad scrolling, dedicated high-priority audio thread, native Wayland tray integration, and heavy PDF rendering optimizations.
Initial public release with save-from-URL offline articles, OPDS 1.2/2.0 catalogs, academic PDF Snip & Explain, Story & Study Companion, and local MCP server.
